speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause given your significant medical history, please describe your specific symptoms and when they first began. Also, could you list your major past medical conditions and current medications?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your symptoms; the "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness are concerning. You mentioned a significant medical history—could you specify what conditions you have been diagnosed with previously? Additionally, did these ataxic symptoms start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

This diagnosis is strongly suggested by your history of uncontrolled Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, a medication known to cause PML, combined with your new onset of gait and limb ataxia. I need to confirm the clinical picture and look for characteristic imaging findings.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.
